body.text: Private gulet charter vs cabin charter — which fits your group?

Choose a private gulet charter if you are traveling with 6 to 12 people, want control over daily swim stops and menus, or prefer quiet anchorages without strangers. Choose a cabin charter if you are a solo traveler or couple willing to trade route flexibility for a per-person weekly rate on a fixed Saturday-to-Saturday itinerary.

Once a group reaches 8 guests, splitting a 4- or 5-cabin private gulet often matches a mid-tier cabin charter per person while letting your captain dodge crowded bays. Cabin charters lock dates and ports ahead, and solo guests face 60–80% single supplements per [2026 pricing data](https://www.smartsailing.co.uk/blog/turkey-gulet-cruise-prices-2026-blue-cruise-charter-cost/).

body.text: What are the best 4-day and 7-day routes (Göcek, Fethiye–Kekova, Bodrum–Gökova)?

For a 4-day mini-cruise, the sheltered Göcek and 12 Islands loop beats every other coastline because passages stay under an hour and seas stay flat. For a full 7-day Blue Cruise, Fethiye–Kekova delivers the strongest mix of swimming and Lycian ruins, while Bodrum–Gökova offers pine-forested bays, wider open-water sails, and Cleopatra Island.
Each corridor carries a distinct rhythm, and matching route length to sea conditions matters more than chasing famous port names:

items: Göcek & 12 Islands (4 days or 7 days): Ideal for first-timers, young kids, or guests prone to seasickness. Short hops link Yassıca Islands, Bedri Rahmi Bay, Cleopatra's Bath, and Tersane Island—covered in detail in our [Göcek sailing guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/gocek-turkey-sailing).

Fethiye–Kekova (7 days round-trip or 4 days one-way): Combines Ölüdeniz, St. Nicholas Island, Kaş, and the protected waters of Kekova and Simena. Expect one longer open-water crossing past Cape Yediburun, which requires early-morning departures when swells are lowest; pair it with our [Kaş & Kalkan guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/kas-kalkan-turkey-guide).

Bodrum–Gökova Gulf (7 days): Runs east from Bodrum into deep green coves like Orak Island, Çökertme, English Harbour, and Sedir (Cleopatra) Island. Stronger afternoon winds make it better for travelers who enjoy real sailing conditions rather than millpond bays.

body.text: How much does a private gulet cost per week including crew and food?

In 2026, a standard 4- to 6-cabin private gulet runs €8,400–€18,650 weekly in shoulder months and €15,750–€36,900 in July–August, while luxury yachts exceed €30,000–€60,000. Charter fees cover the vessel, captain, chef, and deckhands; food, drinks, private marina fees, and crew tips are budgeted separately.

Per [2026 fleet data](https://www.guletvoyage.com/gulet-charter-in-turkey/) and [Albatros Yachting](https://www.albatrosyachting.com/en/gulet-charter-prices-turkey-2026/), full-board provisioning starts around €490/person/week on standard gulets (higher with APA on luxury boats), while July–August rates run 30–40% above June and September ([Barbaros Yachting](https://barbarosyachting.com/blog/yacht-charter-turkey-guide)). Adding Greek islands raises costs 10–20% for customs and port taxes. Always confirm daily air-conditioning hours in writing.
What months have the calmest sailing weather?

Late May, June, September, and early October offer the calmest sailing weather along Türkiye's southwestern coast, pairing warm daytime air (24–30°C) with lighter breezes and uncrowded anchorages. July and August bring the warmest water (26–28°C) but also intense heat above 35°C and strong afternoon Meltemi winds, especially around Bodrum and Datça.

According to [local route meteorological notes](https://www.bluesyachting.com/en/routes/) and [Turkish sailing season guides](https://www.boataround.com/au/blog/turkey-sailing-guide-2025), the prevailing northwest Meltemi typically builds around 11:00 AM to 15–25 knots (occasionally 30 knots near Bodrum and Datça) before dying down at sunset. Captains handle this by motoring early and tucking into sheltered coves before noon. September is the clear sweet spot: sea temperatures remain near their summer peak of 26–28°C while anchorage traffic drops by roughly 40% compared with August, per [Barbaros Yachting](https://barbarosyachting.com/blog/how-to-plan-your-blue-cruise-turkey-adventure).

Choosing a gulet without commission bias can save thousands of euros and prevent mismatches in cabin layout, AC hours, or crew quality. faq.q: Do Turkish gulet charters always run Saturday to Saturday?
faq.a: During peak months (June through September), almost all 7-day private and cabin charters operate Saturday to Saturday. In May and October, owners more readily accept mid-week starts or 3- to 4-night charters.

faq.q: Is alcohol included in gulet full-board packages?
faq.a: Usually not. Standard full-board rates cover breakfast, lunch, afternoon tea, dinner, and sometimes soft drinks, while beer, wine, and spirits are either stocked at supermarket cost plus a service fee or billed from the onboard bar.

faq.q: How much should we tip the crew on a private gulet?
faq.a: Standard practice on the Turkish coast is 5% to 10% of the base charter fee, handed to the captain in cash at the end of the week for equal distribution among the crew.

faq.q: Can we sail from Türkiye to the Greek islands on a 4-day charter?
faq.a: It is rarely worthwhile on a 4-day trip. Customs clearance, transit logs, and crossing times eat into limited days on the water; save Greek island extensions for a 7- to 14-day charter.

faq.q: Do gulets actually sail, or do they mostly use engines?
faq.a: Most gulets are heavy wooden motor-sailers that cruise primarily under engine power for predictable schedules. On windy afternoons with open sea room, crews will hoist sails for an hour or two when conditions allow.

faq.q: Are private gulets suitable for young children?
faq.a: Yes, especially on the sheltered Göcek 12 Islands route. Ask ahead for safety netting along the deck railings, child-sized life jackets, and cabins with twin or triple berth configurations.
